examples.ko: 당뇨가 있는 사람은 인슐린 주사를 맞아요.
examples.en: People with diabetes take insulin shots.
When there isn't enough insulin, blood sugar rises.
The doctor prescribed insulin for me.

examples.ko: 인슐린은 몸에서 혈당을 조절하는 역할을 해요.
examples.en: Insulin plays a role in controlling blood sugar in the body.
I carry an insulin pen in my bag.

examples.ko: 저녁 먹기 전에 인슐린으로 혈당을 맞춰요.
examples.en: Before dinner, I adjust my blood sugar with insulin.

explain: '당뇨', '혈당'과 늘 같이 나오는 의학 단어예요. '인슐린 주사', '인슐린 저항성', '인슐린이 나오다'처럼 써요. 일상 대화에서는 본인이나 가족이 당뇨일 때 주로 들어요.

phrases.example: 아버지는 매일 아침 인슐린 주사를 맞으세요.
phrases.en: My father gets an insulin shot every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 당뇨 치료 이야기에서 가장 자주 나오는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase in talk about diabetes treatment.

phrases.en: My body doesn't produce insulin well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 인슐린을 만들어 내는 것을 쉽게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy way to say the body produces insulin.

phrases.en: The doctor suggested starting insulin treatment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 치료 방법을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used at the hospital to name a treatment method.

explain_en: This medical word almost always appears with '당뇨' (diabetes) and '혈당' (blood sugar). It is used in '인슐린 주사' (insulin shot), '인슐린 저항성' (insulin resistance), and '인슐린이 나오다' (insulin is secreted). In daily talk you mostly hear it when you or a family member has diabetes.

examples.en: If you can't sleep, your concentration drops.

examples.ko: 나이가 들수록 기억력이 저하하는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think memory declines as you get older.
The factory is old, so production efficiency fell.
With the weather getting worse, the ratings will drop.
When my grades fell, my teacher was worried.

examples.ko: 약을 너무 오래 먹으면 면역력이 저하하기도 해요.
examples.en: Taking medicine for too long can also weaken immunity.

explain: 저하하다는 능력, 기능, 수준이 전보다 나빠지거나 떨어질 때 써요. '집중력', '기억력', '면역력', '효율'처럼 눈에 안 보이는 능력과 잘 어울려요. 말할 때는 '떨어지다'가 더 흔하고 저하하다는 글이나 뉴스에서 더 많이 보여요.

phrases.en: When your stamina drops, you catch colds easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: '저하하다'보다 저절로 떨어진다는 느낌이 강하고 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels more like something dropping by itself, and is used more often.

phrases.en: When you lack sleep, your concentration drops.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '저하하다' 대신 쉬운 '떨어지다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday talk, the easier '떨어지다' is used instead of '저하하다'.

phrases.en: I take breaks often so my efficiency doesn't drop.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않도록'을 붙여 나빠지지 않게 조심한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-지 않도록' it means taking care so that something doesn't get worse.

explain_en: 저하하다 is used when ability, function, or level gets worse than before. It goes well with invisible capacities such as '집중력', '기억력', '면역력', and '효율'. In speech '떨어지다' is more common, while 저하하다 is more typical of writing and the news.

t90.ax: I think memory declines as you get older.

examples.ko: 그가 말할 때마다 턱뼈가 움직이는 게 보여요.
examples.en: I can see his jawbone move every time he talks.
I badly injured my jawbone when I fell.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 턱뼈 사진을 보여 주셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor showed me an X-ray of my jawbone.
They say the jawbone where the tooth was pulled has weakened.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 턱뼈가 각져서 인상이 강해 보여요.
examples.en: That actor has an angular jawbone, so he looks strong-featured.
I saw a fossil of an animal's jawbone at the museum.

explain: 몸의 '턱'은 얼굴 아랫부분 전체를 말하고, '턱뼈'는 그 안의 뼈를 가리켜요. 병원이나 치과에서 자주 들을 수 있어요. 사람 얼굴의 윤곽을 말할 때는 '턱선'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I hurt my jawbone while playing soccer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사고나 운동 중에 다친 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for injuries from accidents or sports.

phrases.en: My jawbone broke in an accident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뼈가 부러진 심한 부상을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a serious injury where the bone breaks.

phrases.en: Your jawline is slim, so you look nice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뼈가 아니라 얼굴의 윤곽을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the outline of the face, not the bone.

explain_en: '턱' is the whole lower part of the face, and '턱뼈' points to the bone inside it. You often hear it at hospitals and dentists. When talking about the outline of a face, people also say '턱선'.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 밥 먹을 때 틀니를 끼세요.
examples.en: Grandpa puts in his dentures when he eats.

examples.ko: 틀니가 잘 맞지 않아서 치과에 갔어요.
examples.en: The dentures didn't fit well, so I went to the dentist.
My father got new dentures last year.

examples.ko: 자기 전에 틀니를 깨끗이 닦아야 해요.
examples.en: You have to clean your dentures before going to bed.
Because of the dentures, avoid hard food.
When you get dentures, speaking is awkward at first.

explain: 의학 용어로는 '의치'라고 하지만 일상에서는 '틀니'라고 해요. 몇 개만 끼우는 건 '부분 틀니', 전체는 '완전 틀니'라고 해요. 어르신에게는 '틀니를 하시다'처럼 높여요.

phrases.en: My grandmother has worn dentures since last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어르신에게 쓰는 높임 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A respectful form used for elders.

phrases.example: 이가 몇 개 빠져서 부분 틀니를 했어요.
phrases.en: A few teeth fell out, so I got partial dentures.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이가 몇 개만 없을 때 하는 틀니예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Dentures for when only some teeth are missing.

phrases.en: I take out my dentures and clean them before sleeping.
phrases.nuance_ko: 틀니를 관리할 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used when caring for dentures.

explain_en: The medical term is 의치, but in daily life people say 틀니. A partial set is 부분 틀니 and a full set is 완전 틀니. For elders you raise it: '틀니를 하시다'.

examples.en: The complications of diabetes are scary.

examples.ko: 수술 뒤에 합병증이 생기지 않아서 다행이에요.
examples.en: I am glad no complications appeared after the surgery.

examples.ko: 감기를 오래 두면 합병증으로 이어질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you leave a cold alone for long, it can lead to complications.
The doctor told me to watch out for complications.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 합병증 때문에 한 달 더 입원하셨어요.
examples.en: My grandfather stayed in the hospital another month because of complications.

examples.ko: 합병증을 막으려면 꾸준히 약을 먹어야 해요.
examples.en: To prevent complications, you have to keep taking your medicine.

explain: 합병증은 한 병 때문에 다른 병이나 증상이 따라서 생기는 것이에요. '합병증이 생기다', '합병증을 막다', '합병증이 오다'처럼 써요. '당뇨 합병증'처럼 병 이름과 붙여 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 감기를 오래 앓으면 합병증이 생길 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you have a cold for a long time, complications can develop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병이 나빠지면서 다른 병이 따라 생길 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for when another illness develops because of the first one.

phrases.example: 운동은 합병증을 막는 데 도움이 돼요.
phrases.en: Exercise helps prevent complications.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치료나 관리로 합병증이 안 생기게 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means preventing complications through treatment or care.

phrases.en: You have to be careful about diabetes complications.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병 이름을 앞에 붙여 어떤 병의 합병증인지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a disease name before the word to say which illness the complications come from.

explain_en: Medical: illness arising from or alongside another illness. Hapbyeongjeung is a second illness or symptom that follows from a first illness. It pairs with 생기다, 막다, and 오다, as in 합병증이 생기다. It is often attached to a disease name, as in 당뇨 합병증.

t90.ax: The complications of diabetes are scary.

en: to wear out; to be tattered; to become shabby

examples.en: The clothes wore out from long use.
The shoe soles wore through, so I bought new ones.

examples.ko: 이 가방은 자주 들면 모서리가 해져요.
examples.en: If you carry this bag often, the corners fray.
It's a shame to throw away worn socks.

examples.ko: 책 표지가 해지기 전에 커버를 씌웠어요.
examples.en: I put a cover on before the book jacket wore out.
I wore the jeans until the knees wore out.

explain: 옷, 신발, 가방처럼 오래 써서 닳고 찢어질 때 써요. '낡다'는 오래되어 허름해진 상태이고, '해지다'는 천이나 가죽이 닳아서 올이 풀리거나 구멍이 나는 변화예요. '해가 지다'와 소리는 비슷하지만 달라요.

phrases.example: 해진 신발을 버리고 새 신발을 샀어요.
phrases.en: I threw away my worn-out shoes and bought new ones.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사가 뒤의 명사를 꾸며 닳은 물건을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb modifies the noun to describe a worn-out item.

phrases.example: 이 가방은 오래 써도 안 해져요.
phrases.en: This bag doesn't wear out even after a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 튼튼해서 닳지 않는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it is sturdy and does not wear out.

phrases.en: This desk is very old and worn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래되어 허름해진 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a state of being old and shabby.

explain_en: It is used when clothes, shoes, or bags wear down and fray from long use. 낡다 is the general state of being old and shabby, while 해지다 is the change of fabric or leather wearing thin or tearing. It sounds similar to 해가 지다 (the sun sets) but is unrelated.

t90.ax: The clothes wore out from long use.

examples.ko: 고속도로에서 타이어가 터져서 갓길에 차를 세웠어요.
examples.en: A tire blew out on the highway, so I stopped the car on the shoulder.
You must not drive on the shoulder.
Driving on the shoulder is dangerous, so it is cracked down on.

examples.ko: 차가 고장 나서 갓길에서 견인차를 기다렸어요.
examples.en: My car broke down, so I waited for a tow truck on the shoulder.
I turned on the hazard lights and slowly drove to the shoulder.

examples.ko: 갓길은 급한 차가 설 때만 쓰는 곳이에요.
examples.en: The shoulder is only for emergencies.

explain: 고속도로나 자동차 전용 도로 가장자리에 비상시를 위해 만든 길이에요. 일반 도로의 길 가장자리는 보통 '길가'라고 해요. 평소에는 달리면 안 되고 고장이나 사고 때 차를 세우는 곳이에요.

phrases.en: Parking on the highway shoulder is dangerous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갓길에 차를 세우는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for stopping a car on the shoulder.

phrases.en: When an ambulance comes, you must move over to the shoulder.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길을 비켜 줄 때 가장자리로 간다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means moving to the edge to give way.
phrases.en_equiv: to move over to the shoulder

phrases.en: Flowers have bloomed by the roadside in front of my house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차를 위한 '갓길'과 달리, 사람이 걷는 길 옆 가장자리를 두루 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike 갓길, which is for vehicles, 길가 broadly means the side of a road where people walk.

explain_en: It is the strip at the edge of a highway or expressway made for emergencies. The edge of an ordinary road is usually called '길가'. You should not drive on it normally; it is for stopping when a car breaks down or in an accident.

examples.ko: 급정차 때문에 승객 몇 명이 넘어졌어요.
examples.en: A few passengers fell because of the sudden stop.

examples.ko: 버스 안에서는 급정차에 대비해 손잡이를 잡으세요.
examples.en: On the bus, hold the handle in case of a sudden stop.
Service was briefly delayed by a sudden subway stop.
I screamed, startled by the abrupt stop.
A bus that stops suddenly often is uncomfortable to ride.
After the sudden stop, the driver asked if everyone was okay.

explain: 버스, 지하철, 기차가 갑자기 서는 일이에요. '급정거'와 거의 같은 뜻이라 바꿔 써도 되고, 안내 방송이나 뉴스에서는 '급정차'가 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: The subway suddenly stopped.
phrases.nuance_ko: '급정차'를 동사로 쓴 말이에요. 열차나 버스에 잘 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 급정차, often for trains and buses.

phrases.en: The milk spilled because of the sudden stop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거의 같은 뜻이라 바꿔 써도 되고, 자동차 이야기에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning; more common for cars.

phrases.en: A sudden-stop accident happened and a passenger got hurt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often seen in the news.

explain_en: It is a bus, subway or train stopping suddenly. It is nearly the same as '급정거' and can be swapped, and '급정차' often appears in announcements and news.

examples.en: There are several dump trucks at the construction site.
A dump truck passed by, full of soil.
The child likes toy dump trucks.
I woke up because of the sound of a dump truck.

examples.ko: 덤프트럭은 짐칸을 들어 올려서 짐을 쏟아요.
examples.en: A dump truck raises its bed to unload its cargo.

examples.ko: 길에서 덤프트럭 뒤를 따라가면 먼지가 많아요.
examples.en: If you follow behind a dump truck on the road, there is a lot of dust.

explain: 흙이나 모래를 싣고 짐칸을 기울여 쏟는 트럭이에요. 영어 dump truck에서 온 말이고, 공사장에서 많이 봐요. 아이들 장난감이나 그림책에도 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: My father is a dump truck driver.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used to talk about the job.

phrases.en: The child carries sand with a toy dump truck.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이들 장난감 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears when talking about children's toys.

phrases.en: They load soil onto the dump truck at the construction site.
phrases.nuance_ko: 덤프트럭이 하는 일을 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An expression for what a dump truck does.
phrases.en_equiv: to load soil onto a dump truck

explain_en: It is a truck that carries soil or sand and tips its bed to unload. The word comes from the English 'dump truck', and you often see them at construction sites. It also appears in children's toys and picture books.

examples.en: Cherry blossoms are in full bloom along the road.
You must not park on the side of the road.
Shops by the roadside are very noisy.
I met an old woman selling fruit by the roadside.
Our house is right by the road, so there is a lot of dust.

examples.ko: 도로변을 따라 가로수가 쭉 늘어서 있어요.
examples.en: Street trees line up all along the side of the road.

explain: '길가'가 일상적인 말이고, '도로변'은 차가 다니는 큰길 옆이라는 느낌이 강해요. 안내문, 간판, 뉴스에서 많이 보여요. 비슷한 말로 '길옆'도 있어요.

phrases.en: Many flowers have bloomed by the roadside.
phrases.nuance_ko: '도로변'보다 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More everyday than '도로변'.

phrases.en: I parked my bike beside the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길의 바로 옆을 편하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to say right next to the road.

phrases.en: Stores along the main road are easy to park at.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰길 옆에 있는 가게를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for shops beside a main road.

explain_en: '길가' is the everyday word, while '도로변' strongly suggests the side of a large road for vehicles. You see it on notices, signs and in the news. '길옆' is another similar word.

examples.en: The paving blocks are broken, so it's hard to walk.
Sidewalk blocks are slippery on rainy days.
The district office is laying new sidewalk blocks.
Grass has grown between the paving blocks.
I tripped on a paving block and almost fell.
I walked along the path of red paving blocks.

explain: 길 위에 깔아 놓은 네모난 돌이나 벽돌 모양 포장재를 말해요. 줄여서 '보도블럭'이라고 쓰는 사람도 많지만 표준 표기는 '보도블록'이에요. '보도블록을 깔다', '보도블록이 깨지다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 공사 팀이 길에 보도블록을 깔고 있어요.
phrases.en: The work crew is laying sidewalk blocks on the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길을 새로 만들거나 고칠 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used when building or repairing a path.

phrases.en: A sidewalk block was loose and I almost tripped.
phrases.nuance_ko: 블록이 단단히 박혀 있지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a block isn't firmly set.

phrases.en: Fallen leaves piled up on the sidewalk.
phrases.nuance_ko: '위'를 붙여서 블록이 깔린 길 위의 장소를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 위 refers to the place on top of the paved path.

explain_en: It is the square stone or brick-like paving laid on walkways. Many people write '보도블럭', but the standard spelling is '보도블록'. Common patterns are '보도블록을 깔다' and '보도블록이 깨지다'.

examples.en: This bus has a comfortable ride.

examples.ko: 새 차는 승차감이 부드러워서 멀미가 안 나요.
examples.en: The new car rides smoothly, so I don't get carsick.

examples.ko: 승차감보다 가격이 중요해서 작은 차를 샀어요.
examples.en: Price mattered more than ride comfort, so I bought a small car.
The road is bumpy, so the ride isn't great.
How was the ride in the taxi?
I'm looking for a car with a comfortable ride.

explain: 차, 버스, 기차를 탔을 때 느끼는 편안함을 말해요. '승차감이 좋다/나쁘다/편하다'로 써요. 자동차를 소개하거나 후기를 쓸 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: This train has a comfortable ride.
phrases.nuance_ko: 타고 있는 느낌이 편안하다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise how comfortable it feels to ride.

phrases.en: The road is bumpy, so the ride is uncomfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 타기에 불편할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a ride feels uncomfortable.

phrases.en: This car has a smooth ride.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흔들림 없이 매끄럽게 달릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a vehicle runs smoothly without jolting.

explain_en: It describes how comfortable it feels to ride in a car, bus or train. You say '승차감이 좋다/나쁘다/편하다'. It often appears in car introductions and reviews.

examples.en: The car wouldn't start this morning.
I turned off the engine and got out of the car.
When you press the start button, the lights come on.

examples.ko: 시동이 꺼지는 바람에 길 한가운데서 멈췄어요.
examples.en: The engine died, so we stopped in the middle of the road.

examples.ko: 오토바이는 시동을 걸 때 소리가 커요.
examples.en: A motorcycle is loud when you start the engine.

examples.ko: 요즘 전기차는 시동 소리가 거의 없어요.
examples.en: Electric cars these days make almost no sound when starting.

explain: 차, 오토바이, 기계를 처음 움직일 때 '시동'이라고 해요. '시동을 걸다'와 '시동을 끄다'가 짝이고, 달리다가 멈추면 '시동이 꺼지다'라고 말해요. 일이나 계획을 본격적으로 시작할 때도 '시동을 걸다'를 비유로 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 새 사업이 이제 막 시동을 걸었어요.
phrases.en: The new business has just got going.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이나 계획을 본격적으로 시작할 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively when a job or plan is properly starting.

explain_en: '시동' is starting a car, motorcycle or machine for the first time. '시동을 걸다' and '시동을 끄다' are a pair, and if it stalls while running you say '시동이 꺼지다'. '시동을 걸다' is also often used figuratively for properly starting a job or plan.

examples.en: When it started raining, I turned on the wipers.

examples.ko: 와이퍼가 낡아서 앞이 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: The wipers are worn out, so I can't see ahead well.

examples.ko: 주차 위반 딱지가 와이퍼에 끼워져 있었어요.
examples.en: A parking ticket was tucked under the wiper.
At the shop I replaced the wiper blade rubber with a new one.
Please turn the wiper speed up to fast.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 와이퍼가 얼어붙지 않게 세워 두기도 해요.
examples.en: In winter, people sometimes lift the wipers so they don't freeze to the glass.

explain: 자동차 앞유리의 물기를 닦아 주는 장치예요. 일상에서는 '와이퍼' 그대로 쓰고, 차를 점검할 때 '와이퍼 날'이나 '와이퍼 고무'를 갈아 달라고 말해요. 영어 wiper처럼 다른 닦는 도구 전체를 뜻하지는 않아요.

phrases.en: I turn off the wipers when the rain stops.
phrases.nuance_ko: '켜다'의 반대로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 켜다.

phrases.en: I replaced the wiper blades with new ones.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유리를 닦는 부분을 말하며, 차를 점검할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the part that wipes the glass, often used when servicing a car.

phrases.en: The wipers broke, so I went to the repair shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작동하지 않을 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the wipers no longer work.

explain_en: It is the device that wipes water off a car's windshield. In daily life people just say '와이퍼', and at a repair shop they ask to replace the '와이퍼 날' or '와이퍼 고무'. Unlike the English word, it doesn't refer to wiping tools in general.
